efet_title: CFS announces latest progress of Salt Reduction Scheme in Bread - info.gov.hk
efet_body:
CFS announces latest progress of Salt Reduction Scheme in Bread
CFS announces latest progress of Salt Reduction Scheme in Bread
***************************************************************
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS) of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department announced today (September 29), which is also World Heart Day, the latest progress of the Salt Reduction Scheme in Bread (the Scheme). All products participating in the Scheme have met the voluntary sodium reduction targets, marking the achievements of the joint efforts between the industry and the Government.
The CFS launched the Scheme in 2019, setting voluntary sodium reduction targets for prepackaged white and wholemeal bread to reduce the sodium content in bread. In 2020, the CFS extended the Scheme to non-prepackaged white and wholemeal bread. Currently, seven prepackaged bread manufacturers and 19 non-prepackaged bread manufacturers are participating in the Scheme, providing about 80 types of related bread products that meet the sodium reduction targets on the market. The CFS presented certificates of appreciation to the participating bread manufacturers in recognition of their support.
"The selected products from the prepackaged bread manufacturers and the participating products from the non-prepackaged bread manufacturers met the Scheme's voluntary sodium reduction targets (i.e. the average and maximum levels of sodium content per 100 grams of white bread should not exceed 380 milligrams and 490mg respectively; and the average and maximum levels of sodium content per 100g of wholemeal bread should not exceed 380mg and 470mg respectively). After the implementation of the Scheme, the average sodium content of related bread products decreased by 10 per cent to 17 per cent, with some manufacturers successfully reducing the sodium content of their products by more than 40 per cent," a spokesman for the CFS said.
Sodium is essential for body functions, but excessive intake may increase the risk of developing high blood pressure. Untreated high blood pressure can lead to heart attacks, strokes, kidney failure and more. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends the salt intake for adults should be less than 5g daily (i.e. 2 000 mg of sodium). The Report of Population Health Survey 2020-22 published by the Department of Health revealed that Hong Kong people aged 15 to 84 had an average daily salt intake of 8.4g, which is higher than the WHO's recommendation. As we observe World Heart Day, the CFS reminds the public of the importance of reducing sodium intake in lowering the risk of high blood pressure, thereby promoting heart health and preventing cardiovascular diseases.
The spokesman added that participating bread manufacturers had reduced the sodium content of bread by product reformulation. The CFS also provides training and sodium content testing for bread manufacturers in need and assists them in establishing standard operation procedures for bread to facilitate their product reformulation work.
Ends/Tuesday, September 29, 2026
Issued at HKT 15:00

efet_title: Food Alerts / Allergy Alerts - Not to consume batch of imported spread product suspected to be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes
efet_body:
Not to consume batch of imported spread product suspected to be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes
Issue Date
18.8.2026
Source of Information
Centre for Food Safety
Food Product
Spread product
Product Name and Description
Product name: Ktipiti Extra Red Pepper & Feta Cheese Spread
Brand: L'atelier Blini
Place of origin: France
Net weight: 175 grams
Batch number: 12262661
Use-by date: August 30, 2026
Importer: City Super Limited
Reason For Issuing Alert
The Centre for Food Safety (CFS), through its Food Incident Surveillance System, noted a notification from the Rappel Conso of France that the above-mentioned product is being recalled as it might be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes due to suspected issue with the cold chain.
A preliminary investigation found that the above-mentioned importer had imported into Hong Kong the affected batch of the product concerned.
Listeria monocytogenes can be easily destroyed by cooking but can survive and multiply at refrigerator temperatures. Most healthy individuals do not develop symptoms or only have mild symptoms such as fever, muscle pain, headache, nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea when infected.
However, severe complications such as septicaemia, meningitis or even death may occur in newborns, the elderly and those with a weaker immune system. Although infected pregnant women may just experience mild symptoms generally, the infection of Listeria monocytogenes may cause miscarriage, infant death, preterm birth, or severe infection in newborns.
Action Taken by the Centre for Food Safety
Upon learning of the incident, the CFS immediately contacted local importers to follow up.
As a precautionary measure, the importer concerned has stopped sales and removed from shelves the affected batch of the product and has initiated a recall according to the CFS's instructions.
The CFS has contacted the French authority over the incident and will continue to follow up on the incident and take appropriate action to safeguard food safety and public health. The investigation is ongoing.
Advice to the Trade
Stop using or selling the affected batch of the product immediately.
Advice to Consumers
Stop consuming the affected batch of the product and seek medical treatment if they feel unwell after consuming the product concerned.
Further Information
The CFS press release
Members of the public may call the importer's hotline at 2736 3866 during office hours for enquiries about the recall.
Centre for Food Safety
Food and Environmental Hygiene Department

efet_title: Food Alerts / Allergy Alerts - CFS finds trace amount of formaldehyde in prepackaged rice vermicelli sample
efet_body:
CFS finds trace amount of formaldehyde in prepackaged rice vermicelli sample
Issue Date
29.8.2026
Source of Information
Food Surveillance Programme of the Centre for Food Safety (CFS)
Food Product
Prepackaged rice vermicelli
Product Name and Description
Product name: Hsin Tung Yang Rice Noodles
Brand: Hsin Tung Yang
Place of origin: Taiwan
Distributor: B&S Company
Net weight: 300 grams
Best-before date: April 10, 2029
Reason For Issuing Alert
The CFS collected the above-mentioned sample from an online vendor for testing under its Food Surveillance Programme. The test result showed that the sample contained formaldehyde at a level of 12 parts per million.
Action Taken by the Centre for Food Safety
The CFS has informed the vendor and the distributor concerned of the irregularity, and instructed the distributor concerned to immediately stop sales, remove from shelves, and initiate a recall of the affected batch of the product.
The CFS' follow-up investigation found that the distributor concerned stored about 450 cartons of the affected batch of the product in its warehouse. The CFS has immediately marked and sealed the products concerned.
The CFS has also enhanced formaldehyde testing at the import and retail levels, and has recently collected over 70 food samples, including Chinese white cabbages, vegetables and rice vermicelli, for testing of formaldehyde content. Except for the rice vermicelli sample detected with formaldehyde, no other unsatisfactory testing results have been found so far.
Advice to the Trade
Stop using or selling the affected batch of the product immediately if in possession.
Be cautious about the origins from which the food products are sourced, and should only obtain them from reliable sources.
Advice to Consumers
Not to consume the affected batch of the product concerned.
To patronise reliable restaurants and food retailers. As formaldehyde is water-soluble and highly volatile, washing and cooking food ingredients thoroughly before consumption can reduce the relevant risk.
Further Information
The CFS press release
Members of the public may call the distributor's hotline at 3628 7800 during office hours for enquiries about the recall.
Centre for Food Safety
Food and Environmental Hygiene Department
